scope: Research reconnaissance, 20 search queries plus direct primary-source opens; no formal bibliography or support audit

read_primary_results.work: Aragón, Eberly and Eberly, 1991 Stanford preprint (published 1992)
read_primary_results.locator: printed page 2, PDF page 4: theorem statement; opening proof setup on printed page 3
read_primary_results.read: Theorem statement and opening setup, not a complete proof audit
read_primary_results.result: Claims ordinary NB existence iff divisor-n empirical variance exceeds empirical mean, and uniqueness when it exists
read_primary_results.caveat: This is a preprint. Wang (1996) reports a problem with the 1992 proof; neither the published version nor Wang's full correction was inspected. Do not use this read as a repaired proof.

read_primary_results.work: Sampford (1955), The Truncated Negative Binomial Distribution
read_primary_results.read: Primary scanned pages with embedded OCR, sections 7–8; section 4 moment example also read
read_primary_results.result: Likelihood equations and an alternative solution method; two endpoint conditions suffice for a solution; necessity and uniqueness explicitly remain conjectures there
read_primary_results.caveat: Moment-estimation convergence is not a joint ML uniqueness proof. This historical statement does not establish whether subsequent literature settled the conjectures.

read_primary_results.work: Haslett, Parnell, Hinde and de Andrade Moral (2022), Modelling Excess Zeros in Count Data: A New Perspective on Modelling Approaches
read_primary_results.read: Primary full text, selected sections and displayed decomposition
read_primary_results.result: Zero/nonzero indicator and truncated-count likelihood decomposition; gamma–Poisson NB representation and its zero-probability inequality
read_primary_results.caveat: No general iid joint ZINB existence or uniqueness theorem was located in the inspected material.

read_primary_results.work: Santos Silva (2017), Local Maxima in the Estimation of the ZINB and Sample Selection models
read_primary_results.read: Full slide text, with focus on the ZINB section
read_primary_results.result: Numerical evidence for competing local optima in ZINB regression using covariates
read_primary_results.caveat: Not an iid intercept-only counterexample, not a theorem of equal global maxima.

abstracts_or_metadata_only.observed: Primary journal issue metadata; full-text attempts blocked or challenge pages
abstracts_or_metadata_only.scope: Classical NB reference supplied in task brief; its original NB theorem/proof was not read here

abstracts_or_metadata_only.work: Wang (1996), Estimation problems for the two-parameter negative binomial distribution
abstracts_or_metadata_only.observed: Publisher abstract and metadata through search result
abstracts_or_metadata_only.scope: Abstract reports a major problem with the 1992 proof; full correction not read

abstracts_or_metadata_only.work: Dai, Bao and Bao (2013), Maximum likelihood estimate for the dispersion parameter of the negative binomial distribution
abstracts_or_metadata_only.scope: Abstract asserts uniqueness under a condition and fixed-point convergence when the score root is unique; the condition/theorem was not inspected

abstracts_or_metadata_only.work: Wyshak (1974), A Program for Estimating the Parameters of the Truncated Negative Binomial Distribution (Algorithm AS 68)
abstracts_or_metadata_only.scope: Algorithm record; no theorem or algorithm PDF read. The page's 2018 platform timestamp is not the publication year.

conclusion: No inspected source establishes a general finite-sample iff-C criterion or nondegenerate all-free iid ZINB uniqueness theorem. Search non-discovery is not proof of novelty or absence.
